article.title: 나/이나 aproximación/elección
article.part: Foco y partículas avanzadas — 초점과 고급 조사
article.chapter: Partículas de foco avanzadas — 고급 보조사와 초점

claims.summary: The particle 나/이나 can present an option among several possibilities and, in other contexts, an alternative that the speaker considers sufficient although not especially important or preferred.

After a substantive ending in a vowel, 나 usually appears; after a consonant, 이나. In coordinated structures, it can mark alternatives, such as 커피나 차를 마셔요 (coffee or tea). It can also signify a non-committal or approximate choice within a contextual set.

Examples include 주말에 영화나 볼까요? (Shall we watch a movie or something?), 커피나 차를 주세요 (Give me coffee or tea), 책이나 읽으려고 해요 (I was thinking of reading a book or something), and 학생이 스무 명이나 왔어요 (Twenty students came, nothing less).

links.notes: The description of 나/이나's function in presenting options and alternatives aligns with the explanation provided in the National Institute of Korean Language webpage about '아마도' and speculation expressions.
